sharedRules.name: Artillerist (O)
sharedRules.description: The figure is skilled in the use of artillery pieces. To employ an artillery piece, at least one figure with this Attribute must be within 1" of it. Specific uses of this Attribute will be noted in a given scenario.

sharedRules.name: Miracles
sharedRules.description:
A figure with this Attribute may spend an action to call upon a higher power for miraculous intervention. The figure must make a Courage Check (TN10). If the Check is successful, they may choose one of the Miracles listed below and apply its effects immediately. If the Check is failed, the action is lost and nothing happens. Either way, the figure suffers 1 point of damage from the strain of performing the Miracle.
- Healing: a figure within 8" and line of sight of the figure regains up to 3 points of Health. A figure may not use this Miracle on themselves.
- Courage: a figure within 8" and line of sight of the figure gains +1 Courage for the rest of the game.
- Bless Weapon: a figure within 8" and line of sight of the figure immediately has one of their weapons count as blessed for the rest of the game.

sharedRules.name: Supernatural Veteran (O)
sharedRules.description: This figure has fought and survived many fights against the forces of darkness and has leanred how to properly prepare. If this figure is a soldier, it may select two items from the Special Armoury list, instead of the usual one item. If it is an officer, it may selected three items from the Special Armoury list. This does not increase the figure's overall equipment capacity.

sharedRules.name: Damage Reduction (X)
sharedRules.description: Whenever the figure takes damage, the amount of damage is reduced by X, to a minimum of 0. Damage Reduction does not apply to attacks to which the figure is Allergic.

sharedRules.name: Strong (O)
sharedRules.description: This figure does +1 damage whenever it hits with a Melee Attack.

sharedRules.name: Indefatigable (O)
sharedRules.description: The figure may never be given more than one fatigue token. Any effect that would normally give it a second should be ignored.

sharedRules.name: Medic (O)
sharedRules.description: This figure is skilled in battlefield medicine. If this figure activates within 1" of a friendly figure and does not move, it may spend its action to heal that figure. The figure automatically gains back 2 points of Health. This ability may not be used on the same figure two turns in a row. Additionally, if any member of the unit is reduced to exactly 0 Health (not to -1 or less), then that figure should be laid on its side and left on the table. If a Medic reaches that figure, it may heal it like any other figure. If an enemy figure moves into contact with a figure on its side, it is removed from the table.

sharedRules.name: Combat Rider (O)
sharedRules.description: The figure is trained to fight while mounted on a horse. See full rules for Cavalry on page 65.

sharedRules.name: Master of Cover (O)
sharedRules.description: This figure is skilled at taking advantage of any little bit of cover it can find. If an enemy figure makes a Shooting Attack at this figure, and this figure is in cover, the penalty for the target being in cover is -2 instead of -1.

sharedRules.name: Nimble (O)
sharedRules.description: This figure is skilled at moving quickly through difficult terrain. It suffers no movement penalties for moving through difficult ground.

sharedRules.name: Steady Legs (O)
sharedRules.description: This figure is used to moving and fighting on unsteady platforms, such as the deck of a ship. This figure receives +2 to any Check to avoid falling. Additionally, it never suffers any penalty for fighting on or shooting from an unstead platform.

sharedRules.name: Spells
sharedRules.description:
A figure with this Attribute may spend an action to call upon its supernatural knowledge to try and bend reality in some helpful way. The figure must make a Courage Check (TN10). If the Check is successful, they may choose one of the Spells listed below and apply its effects immediately. If the Check is failed, the action is lost and nothing happens. Either way, the figure suffers 1 point of damage from the strain of performing the Spell.
- Curse: select a figure within line of sight. The figure must make an immediate Courage Check (TN18) or suffer -1 to all die rolls for the rest of the game. A second casting can increase this to -2, but this is the maximum penalty any figure can receive from this spell.
- Manipulate: the play may convert one die in their Fate Pool to another type of die. So, a Power Die could be changed to a Skill Die or Monster Die, etc.
- Enchant weapon: a figure within 8" and line of sight of figure immediately has one of itheir weapons count as enchanted fomr the rest of the game.

sharedRules.name: Expert Climber (O)
sharedRules.description: The figure is a skilled climber, either due to natural abilities or significant amounts of practice. The figure may climb at its normal rate of movement (so 1" of climbing equals 1" of movement).

sharedRules.name: Combat Engineer (O)
sharedRules.description: The figure is skilled in the construction and demolition of battlefield structures, such as bridges and fortifications. This includes knowledge of how to employ gunpowder as an explosive. Specific uses of this Attribute will be noted in a given scenario.

sharedRules.name: Monster Expert
sharedRules.description: If a figure with Monster Expert is part of a unit, the player may add one extra Monster Die to their Fate Pool at the start of each game. Only one extra Monster Die may be gained in this way, no matter how many figures with Monster Expert are part of a unit.

sharedRules.name: Tactician (O)
sharedRules.description: If a figure with Tactician is part of a unit, the player may add one extra Skill Die to their Fate Pool at the start of each game. Only one extra Skill Die may be gained in this way, no matter how many figures with Tactician are part of a unit.

sharedRules.name: Inspiring (O)
sharedRules.description: All allied figures within 6" and line of sight of the figure receive +1 to all Courage Checks. This does not include the figure with Inspiring. A figure may never receive more than +1 to Courage Checks from Inspiring, even if they are within range of multiple figures with the Attribute.

sharedRules.name: Skinshift
sharedRules.description: This figure has the ability to change its form from human to something else. To change, the figure must spend an action and pass a Courage Check (TN14). Alternatively, if the figure ever takes damage, it may optionally attempt the Courage Check without spending an action. If the Courage Check succeeds, the figure should be exchanged for one representing its other form. Skinshifting back into a human follows exactly the same rules, except that the figure may not make a free attempt when it takes damage.

sharedRules.name: Rage
sharedRules.description: The figure has difficulty restraining itself from charging the nearest enemy. When it activates, if it wishes to do anything other than Move towards or Move to Attack the closest enemy figure, it must fire make a Courage Check (TN14). If it succeeds, it may take its actions normally. If it fails, it must move towards or Move to Attack the closest enemy figure.

sharedRules.name: Very Strong
sharedRules.description: This figure does +2 damage whenever it hits with a Melee Attack.

sharedRules.name: Hard to Put Down (O)
sharedRules.description: If a Fate Die is used to negate damage to the figure, the player may roll the die twice and choose which result to take.

sharedRules.name: Cause Confusion
sharedRules.description: Any figure that 'backs off' due to fighting a round of combat with this figure, moves 2" away from the creature in a random direction instead of directly away from the creature.

sharedRules.name: Fear of Fire
sharedRules.description: This figure will not make a Move to Attack any figure that is standing within 2" of a fire or who can make Fire attacks (such as a figure carrying oil and torches). It will strike back if such a figure makes a Move to Attack it. Additionally, ignore such figures when determining the actions of this figure; so, a creature with Fear of Fire will never target a figure that can make fire attacks, even it is the closest unit member.

sharedRules.name: Fey-Touched (O)
sharedRules.description: This figure has some association with the fairy realm, either spending time there, being enchanted by a fairy, or having learned secrets through intense study. All attacks made by this figure count as Enchanted. This attribute may be given to any soldier, but it increases their recruitment cost by +4.

sharedRules.name: Fire Starter (O)
sharedRules.description: This figure may replace either a Move or Shoot action to swap one item of Specialist Equipment it is carrying with Oil and Torches. After the game, they return to their normal equipment.

sharedRules.name: Immune to Missile Weapons
sharedRules.description: This figure is immune to all damage from missile weapons, unless it comes from a source to which it has an allergy.

sharedRules.name: Infectious
sharedRules.description: If a figure is reduced to 0 Health by this figure and must make a survival roll after the game, then a roll of 4-6 on the survival roll is treated as a Slow Recovery result.

sharedRules.name: Reform Over Grave
sharedRules.description: Whenever this figure suffers any damage, it should be immediately moved to its point of origin (generally specified by a scenario).

sharedRules.name: Sow Fear (X)
sharedRules.description: At the end of each turn, all unit members that are within 6" and line of sight of this figure must make a Terror Check with a penalty equal to X.

sharedRules.name: Aquatic
sharedRules.description: This figure naturally inhabits water and will not leave a water terrain feature but will still take the quickest route possible through one to reach their target point. Note: the Lunge ability may be used for an Aquatic creature to attack another figure not in water terrain.

sharedRules.name: Cursethrower
sharedRules.description:
This figure throws cursed objects, which count as a Shooting Attack with a range of 10”. It can run out of ammunition and will need to be reloaded as normal (the figure searches for more ingredients to be thrown, rather than having to actually ‘reload’ an object). The nature of the curse will dictate the effects if it should hit:
- Wasting: It causes no initial Damage, but that figure will take 1 point of Damage each time they activate from now on as the curse draws out their life. If the cursing figure is not slain, then the curse causes the figure to automatically have to make an injury roll at the conclusion of the scenario.
- Burning: Power Die +1 Damage – Roll D10 for each other figure within 3”, on a 7+ they take D5 Damage.
- Slowing: It causes no damage. The figure hit halves all movement until they can pass a TN 11 Courage Test at the start of a following activation.
Each time a figure throws a curse, randomise which effect they have chosen (if they have access to all of them, for instance, roll a D3).

sharedRules.name: Eyeless
sharedRules.description: This figure relies on other senses to hunt its prey and does not require line of sight to the closest figure to target it.

sharedRules.name: Gatecrasher
sharedRules.description: This figure completely ignores movement penalties for low walls, obstacles, and gates, instead simply crashing through them. Mark an area equal to the base size of this figure once it  passes through an obstacle or remove the obstacle from the table if it is narrower than the figure’s base as it is crushed to insignificance. This area may be passed through freely from now on, incurring no movement penalties.

sharedRules.name: Lunge (O)
sharedRules.description: This figure may spend an action to fight a round of melee against a target within 1” instead of needing to be in contact. The combat is resolved as normal. If this model has the Large attribute as well, it may do so within 2” of its target instead. This may be measured vertically as well as horizontally from the tallest reasonable point of the model.

sharedRules.name: Non-Aggressive
sharedRules.description: This figure will only become aggressive if it feels threatened. When it appears on a table edge it will move in a straight line towards the opposite edge, leaving once it can move off. If a firearm is fired within 12” of it, or it begins an activation with a soldier within 6” of it, it will immediately become aggressive and target that model until either one is destroyed. It will then continue to follow the wandering monster rules as normal after that. If left alone, it will simply leave the battlefield.

sharedRules.name: Swimmer (O)
sharedRules.description: This figure does not count any water terrain feature as difficult ground and, when in water, may choose to count as being in cover. If it ever uses a water terrain feature as cover during the course of a game however, it may no longer use any ranged weapons for the duration of the encounter as they become fouled with water.

sharedRules.name: Trample
sharedRules.description: If this figure strikes a model in melee that is of a smaller size (i.e. a Large model striking a model without Large), it will knock it down in addition to doing Damage. A knocked down figure must forfeit its move action to stand up during its following activation and, if defending from a melee attack while knocked-down, will suffer -2 Defence.

sharedRules.name: Allergy to X
sharedRules.description: If a figure also has the Indestructible or Damage Reduction Attribute, then those Attributes do not apply to any attack made with the Allergy. So, a figure that is Indestructible and has an Allergy to silver, takes normal damage from attacks made with silver. In theory, a figure can be allergic to anything, but the most common Allergies for the game are blessed weapons, cold iron, enchanted weapons, fire, silver, and salt.

sharedRules.name: Quick Healing
sharedRules.description: This figure regains up to 2 points of Health every time it activates, up to its starting value.

sharedRules.name: Amphibious
sharedRules.description: This figure never suffers any penalties for being in the water, automatically passes any checks made for the purposes of swimming or movement in the water, and never suffers any damage from drowning.

sharedRules.name: Ancient Spells
sharedRules.description:
A figure with this Attribute may spend an action to call upon its supernatural knowledge to try and bend reality in some useful way. The figure must make a Courage Check (TN10). If the Check is successful, it may choose one of the spells listed below and apply its effects immediately. If the check is failed, the action is lost and nothing happens. Either way, the figure suffers 1 point of damage from the strain of performing the spell.
- Control Creature – If this unit currently has no Monster Dice in their Fate Pool, add 1 Monster Die.
- Flaming Weapon – Select a figure within 8” and line of sight. All that figure’s Melee Attacks do +1 damage and count as Fire attacks for the rest of the game.
- Viper – Place a viper (see page 58) within 3” of this figure, but at least 1” away from any other figure. It follows the normal rules for a creature.

sharedRules.name: Bestow Mummy's Curse
sharedRules.description: Any unit member damaged by this figure must roll for the Mummy’s Curse after the game.

sharedRules.name: Combustion
sharedRules.description: When this figure is hit with a Fire attack that does three or more points of damage, it combusts, becoming a living torch. This figure suffers two additional points of fire damage every time it activates. Any figure contacted by this figure immediately suffers one point of fire damage. The only way this burning can be stopped is to completely dowse or submerge the figure in water, deprive it of oxygen by covering it or burying it, or the use of magic.

sharedRules.name: Deathroll
sharedRules.description: If this figure is in water and it makes a Melee Attack against another figure that cause one or more points of damage, that figure must make an immediate Courage Check (10). If the figure fails, it suffers drowning damage equal to the amount by which it failed as it is spun about under the water. If the Check is passed, no additional damage is suffered.

sharedRules.name: Leap
sharedRules.description: If a player uses a Monster Die to control the movement of this creature, the player may choose to make it Leap. It suffers -2 Move but can move over any terrain that is less than 3” high. Additionally, if the Leap is a Move to Attack, this figure gains +1 Fight and Strong for this one attack.

sharedRules.name: Maximum Damage (X)
sharedRules.description: If this figure hits with an Attack, it cannot cause more than X points of damage. If the attack would normally cause more than X, reduce the damage caused by the attack to X.

sharedRules.name: Poor Senses
sharedRules.description: This figure cannot see or otherwise detect a figure that is more than 10” away. Thus, it cannot draw line of sight to them, and will never factor them in when determining its actions.

sharedRules.name: Small
sharedRules.description: This figure’s small size makes it difficult to hit with Shooting Attacks. All Shooting Attacks suffer a -2 against it.

sharedRules.name: Submerge
sharedRules.description: While this figure is in water, figures more than 6” away cannot draw line of sight to it.

sharedRules.name: Suppress Combustion
sharedRules.description: If this figure has combusted, then every time it activates, before it takes damage from combustion, it should roll a Check. If the result is 14 or higher, the combustion has been supressed and the fire extinguished. It takes no further damage from this combustion. The figure is still susceptible to combusting again following the normal rules.

sharedRules.name: Venomous
sharedRules.description: Any figure damaged by this creature, but not reduced to 0 Health, must make an immediate Courage Check (TN14). If the roll fails, the figure is poisoned. It suffers -2 Move and a -1 to all Checks. This lasts until the end of the game, or until the figure receives any kind of healing that increases their current Health.

sharedRules.name: Experience in the Desert
sharedRules.description: The special rules Extreme Temperatures, Loose Sand, and Thirst do not apply to this figure.

sharedRules.name: Chilling Touch
sharedRules.description: When making a Melee Attack, the figure ignores any armour worn by its target and does an additional +1 damange.

sharedRules.name: Demonic Fire
sharedRules.description: The figure is capable of making Shooting Attacks at a range of up to 12". These attacks are enchanted and cause +2 damage. Demonic Fire does not require Reloading.

sharedRules.name: Ethereal
sharedRules.description: The figure can see and move through terrain as though it is not there, and never suffers any Speed penalties for moving over difficult ground, thrugh obstacles, or for climbing.

sharedRules.name: Flying
sharedRules.description: The figure can fly, either by natural or supernatural means. The figure may Move over or up any terrain without any movement penalty.

sharedRules.name: Great Faith (O)
sharedRules.description: The figure has an extremely strong faith in a higher power that sometimes allows it to damage creatures that would otherwise be immune to their weapons. The figure's weapons always count as blessed.

sharedRules.name: Hypnotic
sharedRules.description: Any opponent that attempts to make a Move to Attack against this figure must first make a Courage Check (TN12). If the Check is failed, the opponent still makes the Move, but does not make a Melee Check. The figure is still allowed to Strike Back or Back Off, as usual.

sharedRules.name: Inimical to Technology
sharedRules.description: Any attempt to use technology within 6" of this creature fails. In game terms, this includes all firearms and artillery, so all figures making Shoot Checks within 6" automatically miss their target.

sharedRules.name: Indestructible
sharedRules.description: The figure is immune to all damage from any source, unless it comes from a source to which it has an Allergy.

sharedRules.name: Irritant
sharedRules.description: The figure will never attack. If it moves into contact with an enemy figure, give the enemy figure a fatigue token, but move the creature 1" directly back. If attacked, the creature will always Back Off.

sharedRules.name: Large
sharedRules.description: The figure is so big that it is an easy target. All Shooting Checks made against it are at +1.

sharedRules.name: Quick Load (O)
sharedRules.description: In an emergency, this figure is practiced at loading a weapon extremely quickly. This figure may fire an unloaded weapon, but suffers -2 on the Shooting Attack. Additionally, the shooter suffers a critical failure on a roll of 2-4.

sharedRules.name: Rock Hurler
sharedRules.description: This figure always counts as armed with a loaded projectile weapon, as it can pick up just about any object and hurl it with enough force to do significant damange. Damage from a hurled rock is equal to the Power Die. The maximum range is 12".

sharedRules.name: Soul Shear
sharedRules.description: If this figure damages another figure in a Melee Attack, the damaged figure must make a Terror Check with the modifier equal to the damage taken. So, if a figure suffers 4 damage from a figure with Soul Shear, it must make a Terror Check -4.

sharedRules.name: Unflappable (O)
sharedRules.description: This figure has an internal strength that sometimes allows it to face the most horrific of dangers. Any time this figure fails a Courage Check (including Terror Checks), the play may spend any die for the Fate Pool to have the figure pass automatically (or to get a No Effect for a Terror Check).

sharedRules.name: Weakened by Faith
sharedRules.description: If this figure makes a Melee Attack against a figure with a holy symbol, then it suffers a -3 to its Melee Check.

sharedRules.name: Brittle
sharedRules.description: If struck by a heavy weapon, or if struck or shot with a critical hit, this monster is considered to have been pulverised into dust. Remove the monster from the table.

sharedRules.name: Curse of the Evil Eye
sharedRules.description: Known in Italian as malocchio, those who receive this curse suffer from a string of terrible luck – it can even be dangerous if not remedied. When making an Attack action against a figure with this attribute, any roll of a 9 or 10 on either the Skill Die or Power Die must be rerolled. The second roll stands. When the figure who has this attribute makes an Attack action against a player’s figure and rolls either a 1 or a 2, reroll the dice. The second roll stands. Figures with the Great Faith attribute, or those with a Holy Symbol, are immune to the effects of this curse and will Attack and be Attacked as normal by a figure with the Curse of the Evil Eye attribute.

sharedRules.name: Dark Gift
sharedRules.description: Upon activation, if this trigger is relevant, this necromancer must make a courage check (TN10). If it passes, any undead creature (Revenant, Skeleton, Skeletal Soldier, Ghost, Spectral Soldier, Mummy, or Grave Golem) in line of sight and within 6” that has suffered damage recovers 2 Health (cannot exceed full Health). If, for some reason, this attribute cannot be used (all undead out of range or out of sight), and the necromancer has suffered damage, then the necromancer recovers 2 Health (cannot exceed full Health). If no undead are in sight, or out of range, and the necromancer has not taken any damage, it must then use its Raise the Dead attribute instead, regardless of distance to any players’ figures.

sharedRules.name: Light Infantry Training (O)
sharedRules.description: This figure does not suffer a -1 modifier when Moving and Shooting, but can only move at a Speed of 4 when utilising this ability.

sharedRules.name: Quick to Run
sharedRules.description: Any time this character receives damage to their health, roll a Terror Check.

sharedRules.name: Paralyse
sharedRules.description:
If the figure with this attribute causes damage to another figure in Melee Combat, that figure has succumbed to a horrific nightmare, despite being wide
awake. They are ‘Paralysed’ as is listed on the Terror Check Table (The Silver Bayonet). The target must follow the ‘Paralysed’ rules accordingly.

sharedRules.name: Raise the Dead
sharedRules.description:
Upon activation, if this trigger is relevant, the figure that has this attribute may make a roll against the Raise the Dead Table to see what creature they summon. The summoned monster is placed anywhere within 3” of the
necromancer in a random location.


R A I S E T H E D E A D T A B L E
Die Roll Summoned Creature
1–5 Skeletal Soldier
6–8 Revenant (The Silver Bayonet, page 145)
9 Black Dog (The Silver Bayonet, page 138)
10 Ghost (The Silver Bayonet, page 140)

sharedRules.name: Sneak (O)
sharedRules.description:
Once per scenario, this figure can move unseen if it does not attack this turn and stays its own movement range away from any hostile character or monster. This figure stays in sneak after its movement until its next activation or if an enemy moves into its movement range. Whilst in sneak, no enemy can draw line of sight to this figure unless:


1. The target is not behind cover.
2. The target is within its movement range from the figure with this attribute.


If the figure with this attribute is behind substantial Cover (such as a wall or debris), even whilst within melee range, it is assumed that they cannot be seen.


Players are encouraged to agree on whether a piece of cover qualifies before the figure moves into contact with it.

sharedRules.name: Blessed of Britain
sharedRules.description: Once per game, if this figure is on the table, the player may convert one Power Die in their Fate Pool into a Skill Die, or vice versa. If this is done, this figure gains back up to 3 points of lost Health.

sharedRules.name: Chaotic
sharedRules.description: If a player attempts to use a Monster Die to influence this creature’s movement, roll the die. On a 4 – 10, the die works as normal. On a 1–3, the Monster Die is discarded with no effect.

sharedRules.name: Command Skeletal Roman Legionary
sharedRules.description: While a figure possessing this Attribute is on the table, all Skeletal Roman Legionaries gain +1 Speed, +1 Courage, and the Strong Attribute.

sharedRules.name: Ethereal Cavalry
sharedRules.description: All the cavalry rules for Melee and Shooting apply to this figure, but none of the movement rules. Instead, this figure counts as having the Ethereal attribute and can move through walls, buildings, and even up stairs with no penalty. Ethereal cavalry can never dismount.

sharedRules.name: Flitting Movement
sharedRules.description: When activating a figure with this Attribute, first move it 6” in a random direction, then determine its actions. This random movement cannot take it off the table. If it moves into another figure, continue to move it along the same line until they are at least 1” away from all other figures.

sharedRules.name: Frenzy
sharedRules.description: If this figure makes a Melee Attack that causes damage, then its opponent may only Back Off, it may not Strike Back. Additionally, if a player wishes to use a Monster Die to change the movement of this creature, it may only do so if the new movement is a Move to Attack.

sharedRules.name: Head-Taker
sharedRules.description: Any unit member reduced to 0 Health by this figure suffers -1 to its roll on the Injury and Death Table after the game.

sharedRules.name: Induce Terror
sharedRules.description: Any time a figure activates within line of sight of this creature, it must make a Terror Check. If the figure is more than 8” away, it is a Terror Check (-1). If the figure is 8” or closer, it’s a Terror Check (-3).

sharedRules.name: Powerful Jaws
sharedRules.description: When this figure hits with a Melee Attack, it uses the higher result from either the Power Die or Skill Die to determine damage.

sharedRules.name: Reanimate
sharedRules.description: If this figure is reduced to 0 Health by a Blessed or Fire Attack, remove it from the table as normal. Otherwise, leave the figure on the table on its side. At the end of each turn, roll a die. On a ‘10’, stand this figure back up and give it 1 Health. It will follow its normal rules. If a figure with a Blessed or Fire Attack moves into contact with this figure while it is on its side, remove it from the table.

sharedRules.name: Scourge of Britain
sharedRules.description: Once per game, if this figure is on the table, the player may convert one Skill Die or Fate Die in their Fate Pool into a Monster Die. If this is done, this figure gains back up to 3 lost Health.

sharedRules.name: Weather Control
sharedRules.description:
At the end of each turn that this figure is on the table, roll a die on the Weather Control Table below and apply the effects for the next turn.


WEATHER CONTROL TABLE
Die Roll | Effect
1–3 | Wind: All Shooting Attacks are at -2.
4–6 | Rain: All Shooting Attacks that roll nothing but ‘1 and 2’s on the dice are treated as critical failures.
7–8 | Ice: All Sprint checks are at -4. Additionally, if the total of the roll is 0 or less, the figure falls over. It does not move any additional amount for the Sprint and immediately suffers 2 points of damage. This effect lasts until the end of the scenario.
9–10 | Lightning Strike: Roll the Power Die. The unit member standing closest to the figure with the Weather Control Attribute immediately suffers this amount of damage. The player whose figure suffers the strike may use a Power Die from their Fate Pool to reroll this damage.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: Cartridge Box to reload, ignore Armour (1), includes bayonet (Hand Weapon).

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: A box filled with cartridges (basically a musket ball and gunpowder in a paper roll). It is necessary to carry a cartridge box to reload any rifle or musket.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: -1 Shoot, 2 potential targets, ignore Armour (1), Shot Bag to reload, can be used as Improvised Weapon.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: Gives the wearer Armour (1) and -1 Speed.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: Maximum 2 per figure, ignore Armour (1), can be used as Improvised Weapon.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: Cartridge Box to reload, ignore Armour (1), includes bayonet (Hand Weapon).

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: A large bag or pouch designed to carry ammunition and gunpowder for reloading a blunderbuss.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: This is an upgrade to a cartridge box, shot bag, or pistol. A figure with cold iron shot may declare they are using it whenever they make a Shooting Check. It does not change the attributes of the weapon as listed on the Weapons and Armour Table, but does make it more effective against some monstrous creatures, such as goblins. However, cold iron shot is brittle and likely to break up when firing. If the figure rolls a 1 on either die for their Shooting Check, the shot misses automatically and no dice from the Fate Pool may be used to reroll. If the figure rolls a 1 on both dice, then the gun has fouled and is unusable for the rest of the game.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: This is an upgrade to a hand weapon, heavy weapon, fencing weapon, or bayonet. A figure with cold iron shot may declare they are using it whenever they make a Shooting Check. It does not change the attributes of the weapon as listed on the Weapons and Armour Table, but does make it more effective against some monstrous creatures, such as goblins. However, cold iron weapons are more brittle than their steel counterparts. If the figure rolls a 1 on either die for their Melee Check, the attack misses automatically and no dice from the Fate Pool may be used to reroll. If the figure rolls a 1 on both dice, then the weapon breaks and is unusable for the rest of the game.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Carrying a holy symbol confers special protections against some creatures. Holy symbols take up one equipment slot.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: A figure with oil and torches may spend an action to light a torch. While a figure is carrying a torch, it counts as being armed with an improvised weapon and may not use any weapon that takes up two or more equipment slots. Many creatures that are immune to normal weapons, such as vampires and werewolves, can be hurt by fire. Oil and torches take up one equipment slot.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: A figure equipped with a salt bag may load salt into a firearm. Salt won't do any damage against most living creatures, but it is useful against some monstrous creatures, such as ghosts and demons. A figure with a salt bag may declare they are using it whenever they use a firearm; however, if the figure rolls a 1 on either die for their Shooting Check, the shot misses automatically and no dice from the Fate Pool may be used to reroll. If the figure rolls a 1 on both dice, the gun has fouled and is unusable for the rest of the game. A salt bag takes up one equipment slot.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: This is an upgrade to a cartridge box, shot bag, or pistol. It doesn't change the attributes of the weapon as listed on the Weapons and Armour Table, but does make it more effective against some creatures, such as werewolves.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: This is an upgrade to a hand weapon, heavy weapon, fencing weapon, or bayonet. It doesn't change the attributes of the weapon as listed on the Weapons and Armour Table, but does make it more effective against some creatures, such as werewolves.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: Given that these weapons do not use physical ammunition, these firearms do not have to be reloaded; however, they can only be fired once per activation, just like a regular musket. They do not require a Reloading action, permitting the wielder to fire and move in the same turn. When making a Shooting Attack, the figure ignores any armour worn by its target and does an additional +1 damage. Targets behind Cover will still receive a Cover bonus as normal, unless the players choose to use the Hard Mode rules instead, in which case Cover is also ignored.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: Skeletal soldiers carry with them what remains of their equipment, including their firearms or hand weapons. Like good soldiers, they won’t leave them behind, even in the afterlife! However, any guns carried do not function, as it is assumed the barrels are full of dirt, crud, and rust, and all mechanisms are locked in place due to neglect and being left out in the elements. All firearms are therefore treated as Hand Weapons. In addition, any blunt or bladed weapon carried by a skeleton, regardless of size, is considered rusted and in disrepair, and therefore falls under the Hand Weapon category.

profiles.name: Lupo Mannaro (Calabrian Werewolf)
profiles.comment: When in Werewolf form, the Lupo Mannaro gains +2 Defence, +3 Health, and gains the attributes Strong, Indefatigable, Quick Healing, and Hard to Put Down, but it can no longer investigate clue markers.
